🤖 នៅពេលកូដ និងអេឡិចត្រូនិករួមគ្នា "Robot Dog" ក៏ចាប់ផ្តើមដើរ - When coding meets engineering, a Robot Dog comes to life!

ការរៀនបែប Hands-on Learning នេះជួយអភិវឌ្ឍជំនាញ Robotics, Coding, Problem-Solving និង Teamwork ដែលជាមូលដ្ឋានសម្រាប់វិស្វករ និងអ្នកបង្កើតបច្ចេកវិទ្យានាពេលអនាគត។

EN: In our STEM Robotics Engineering Program, students are building and testing a Quadruped Robot (Robot Dog) through hands-on learning. By integrating electronics, servo motor control, and coding, they gain practical engineering experience while developing skills in robotics, problem-solving, and teamwork.

sections.heading: ភាសាខ្មែរ៖
sections.text: 🤖 ការធ្វើបទបង្ហាញ៖ Smart Lock System – តើ Matrix Keypad និង Servo Motor អាចធ្វើការរួមគ្នា ដើម្បីបង្កើតប្រព័ន្ធសោឆ្លាតវៃ បានយ៉ាងដូចម្តេច? – Smart Lock System — How can a Matrix Keypad and Servo Motor work together to create a smart locking system?
សិស្សបានធ្វើបទបង្ហាញអំពីគម្រោង Smart Lock System ដែលបញ្ចូលគ្នានូវ Matrix Keypad, Servo Motor, Electronics និង Programming ដើម្បីបង្កើតប្រព័ន្ធសោឆ្លាតវៃ។

បន្ថែមពីនេះសិស្សក៏បានបង្ហាញអំពីគោលការណ៍ដំណើរការរបស់ Matrix Keypad ដែលអនុញ្ញាតឱ្យអ្នកប្រើបញ្ចូលលេខកូដ (Password) តាមរយៈគ្រាប់ចុច។ ពួកគេក៏បានពន្យល់អំពីការតភ្ជាប់ជួរដេក និងជួរឈរ (Rows and Columns) របស់ Keypad និងរបៀប ដែលប្រព័ន្ធអាចអានការចុចគ្រាប់ចុចនីមួយៗ ដើម្បីទទួលបានទិន្នន័យបញ្ចូល។

បន្ថែមពីនេះសិស្សក៏បានបង្ហាញអំពីគោលការណ៍ដំណើរការរបស់ Matrix Keypad ដែលអនុញ្ញាតឱ្យអ្នកប្រើបញ្ចូលលេខកូដ (Password) តាមរយៈគ្រាប់ចុច។ ពួកគេក៏បានពន្យល់អំពីការតភ្ជាប់ជួរដេក និងជួរឈរ (Rows and Columns) របស់ Keypad និងរបៀប ដែលប្រព័ន្ធអាចអានការចុចគ្រាប់ចុចនីមួយៗ ដើម្បីទទួលបានទិន្នន័យបញ្ចូល។

ជាចុងក្រោយរៀបរាប់អំពី Servo Motor ដែលជាម៉ូទ័រអាចគ្រប់គ្រងមុំបង្វិល បានយ៉ាងជាក់លាក់។ តាមរយៈការតភ្ជាប់សៀគ្វី (Wiring) និងការសរសេរកម្មវិធី (Coding) Servo Motor អាចបង្វិល ដើម្បីធ្វើសកម្មភាពចាក់សោ និងដោះសោតាមលក្ខខណ្ឌ ដែលបានកំណត់ក្នុងកម្មវិធី។

sections.heading: English:
sections.text: Project Presentation — Smart Lock System: How can a Matrix Keypad and Servo Motor work together to create a smart locking system?

As part of the Robotics Engineering course, students presented their Smart Lock System project, integrating a Matrix Keypad, Servo Motor, electronics, and programming to build a smart locking mechanism. They explained the key components, including the Arduino main board, matrix keypad, servo motor, and power supply, highlighting the role of each component in the system.

The students demonstrated how the Matrix Keypad allows users to enter a password using its buttons. They also explained the keypad's row-and-column wiring configuration and how the system reads individual key presses as input data.

In addition, the students introduced the Servo Motor, which provides precise control over rotational position. Through circuit wiring and coding, the servo motor can rotate to perform locking and unlocking actions according to the programmed conditions.

title: Big ideas start with small steps in code.

summary: A sequence, a repeat and a question: discover how simple programming ideas help young learners turn curiosity into action.

sections.heading: Give an idea a clear sequence
sections.text: Coding starts with thinking about what should happen, and in what order. A learner might break a movement or a simple animation into smaller instructions. Block-based programming makes those instructions visible, creating a useful starting point for exploring sequences, loops and decisions.

sections.heading: Predict, run and notice
sections.text: Before running a program, ask what you expect it to do. Then compare that prediction with the result. If something behaves differently, change one instruction and try again. This habit turns an unexpected result into a question to investigate rather than a reason to stop.

កម្មវិធីនេះត្រូវបានរចនាឡើងដើម្បីភ្ជាប់ចន្លោះរវាងទ្រឹស្តី និងការអនុវត្តជាក់ស្តែង ទាក់ទងនឹងការហោះហើរ យល់ដឹងអំពីមុខងារ ការផ្គុំដំឡើង និងបញ្ជាដូចជា៖

🚀ការសង់ផ្គុំតម្លើង (Assembly)៖ សិស្សបានទទួលបទពិសោធន៍ផ្ទាល់ដៃក្នុងការផ្គុំគ្រឿងបន្លាស់ ការផ្សារសៀគ្វី និងការយល់ដឹងពីអេឡិចត្រូនិកដែលធ្វើឲ្យការហោះអាចទៅរួច។

🚀ការហោះហើរនិម្មិត (Simulation)៖ មុនពេលប្រថុយនឹងឧបករណ៍ពិត សិស្សបានហ្វឹកហាត់ជាច្រើនម៉ោងលើ Simulator ដើម្បីបង្កើតការចងចាំ និងរៀនពីរូបវិទ្យានៃការហោះក្នុងបរិស្ថានសុវត្ថិភាព។

🚀ការហោះហើរពិត (Real Flight)៖ ចំណុចសំខាន់នៃវគ្គសិក្សាគឺការហ្វឹកហាត់ជាក់ស្តែងនៅទីលាន។ ការរៀនដោះស្រាយអថេរក្នុងពិភពពិតដូចជា ខ្យល់ ការរំខានសញ្ញា និងការយល់ដឹងពីជម្រៅ គឺជាជំនាញដែលអាចរៀនបានតែនៅលើអាកាស។

This program was designed to bridge the gap between theory and reality, and the results have been outstanding. We focused on a comprehensive curriculum that covered three critical pillars of drone operation

✅ Assembly: Students got hands-on experience assembling components, soldering, and understanding the electronics that make flight possible.

✅ Simulator: Before risking hardware, students logged hours on simulators to build muscle memory and learn the physics of flight in a safe environment.

✅ Real Flight: The practical field training. Learning to handle real-world variables like wind, signal interference, and depth perception.

📢 NEXT COURSE COMING SOON!

author: RobotYOUNG Academy
title: Learning doesn’t stop at the classroom door.
alt: Students working on robots together in the classroom
summary: From hands-on projects to Cambodia Robotics Olympiad participation, our learners take their ideas into the wider robotics community.

sections.heading: Ideas become something you can build
sections.text: Robotics brings science, technology, engineering and mathematics together. At RobotYOUNG Academy, learners explore these subjects through hands-on projects, turning ideas into builds they can test and improve.

images.alt: Two students assembling electronics at a table with tools and a laptop
images.caption: Building with electronics and tools.

images.alt: An instructor guiding learners assembling electronics on blue work mats
images.caption: Practical guidance while building.

sections.heading: A wider community of makers
sections.text: Learning reaches beyond classroom activities through student projects and Cambodia Robotics Olympiad participation. Explore the academy’s project page for a closer look at what young makers are working on.

author: RobotYOUNG Academy
title: Build. Test. Learn. Try again.
alt: A student wearing glasses connecting wires on a green robot with yellow wheels
summary: A robot’s first attempt is only the beginning. Small tests help makers understand what works and what to improve next.

sections.heading: Start with one clear goal
sections.text: A robotics project becomes easier to explore when its goal is specific. Can the robot move forward, stop where intended or respond to an input? Choosing one behavior gives a learner something concrete to build toward and a clear result to observe.

sections.heading: Change one thing at a time
sections.text: When a build does not behave as expected, several explanations may be possible: its assembly, connections or instructions. With guidance, learners can check one part at a time and repeat the same test. Changing only one thing makes it easier to see which adjustment helped.

images.alt: Students testing a small robot on cardboard roads beside wired electronics and model buildings
images.caption: Testing a robot in a model environment.

sections.heading: Keep the learning, not just the finished build
sections.text: A short note or sketch can capture what was tried, what happened and what to try next. The finished robot matters, but so does the process of asking questions and improving an idea. Visit the academy’s project page to explore the hands-on side of robotics learning.

author: RobotYOUNG Academy
title: Better ideas grow together.
alt: Two learners reviewing printed instructions together at a laptop
summary: Sharing a plan, listening to another idea and explaining a result are part of the learning—not just the work around it.

sections.heading: Make space for another perspective
sections.text: Working together gives learners a chance to compare different ways of solving the same problem. One person might notice a detail in the instructions while another suggests a new approach. Taking time to listen can help a team see possibilities that one maker might miss.

images.alt: Two students working at a laptop beside wheeled robots and electronics
images.caption: Sharing a workspace and exploring robotics together.

sections.heading: Share the tools and the thinking
sections.text: A collaborative activity can include planning, assembling, programming and checking results. Taking turns gives each learner a chance to contribute beyond a single task. Explaining a choice to a teammate also helps make the reasoning behind it clearer.

images.alt: Two students assembling electronics at a table with tools and a laptop
images.caption: Hands-on teamwork with electronics and tools.

sections.heading: Celebrate a useful question
sections.text: What did we expect? What did we notice? What should we try next? These questions keep a shared project moving without requiring every answer straight away. Browse life at the academy for a glimpse of learners building, exploring and working alongside one another.

author: RobotYOUNG Academy
title: Small circuits. Big questions.
alt: A learner working on a circuit board on a blue electronics mat beside a laptop
summary: Explore how connections, components and careful observation help learners make sense of electronics.

sections.heading: Follow the connections
sections.text: An electronics project is a chance to ask how individual parts work together. With guidance, learners can compare a diagram with a physical build, identify connections and describe the role of each component. Understanding the arrangement matters more than simply copying it.

images.alt: An adult guiding a student working on a small circuit board at a table
images.caption: Looking closely at a circuit with guidance.

sections.heading: Observe before changing
sections.text: Before adjusting a build, pause to describe what happened and what was expected. A clear question gives the next check a purpose. Always follow the instructor’s guidance for powering, connecting and handling electronics.

author: RobotYOUNG Academy
title: Every build has a story to share.
alt: Two students presenting with a laptop and microphone beside a projected programming screen
summary: Explaining a project helps a young maker connect the idea, the process and the result—not just show the finished robot.

sections.heading: Start with the problem
sections.text: A useful project explanation begins with what the maker wanted to achieve. Describe the goal in everyday words, then show how the build responds to it. A sketch or demonstration can make a technical idea easier for someone else to follow.

sections.heading: Share what changed
sections.text: The first idea and the finished project may look different. Explaining a test, an unexpected result and the adjustment that followed makes that learning visible. Leave room for questions: another person may notice a possibility worth exploring next.

author: RobotYOUNG Academy
title: A small model opens up big ideas.
alt: Students and an instructor demonstrating a cardboard model city with robots and electronics
summary: A model road, a moving robot and a practical question can bring several STEM ideas into one hands-on project.

sections.heading: Make an idea visible
sections.text: A model gives a team a shared place to explore an idea. Cardboard roads and buildings can help learners describe routes, movement and the space a robot needs. The model does not have to be elaborate to make a question concrete.

images.alt: Students testing a small robot on cardboard roads beside wired electronics and model buildings
images.caption: Trying an idea in a model environment.

sections.heading: Test one part of the journey
sections.text: Choose a short route or a single behavior before trying a complete system. Observe the result, compare it with the plan and discuss the next adjustment. Small tests make it easier to understand how design and programming work together.

author: RobotYOUNG Academy
title: An unexpected result is a starting point.
alt: A student typing code on a laptop beside a wheeled robot and white enclosure
summary: Debugging begins with noticing a difference, asking a clear question and trying a focused change.

sections.heading: Describe what happened
sections.text: When a program does something unexpected, describe the behavior before making changes. What instruction was running? What should have happened instead? A specific description helps narrow the search and makes it easier to ask someone else for help.

sections.heading: Keep the comparison fair
sections.text: Try one change and repeat the same scenario. If several instructions change at once, it becomes harder to know which one affected the result. Keep a short note of each attempt so useful discoveries are not lost between tests.

author: RobotYOUNG Academy
title: Ask about the journey, not just the answer.
alt: Children gathered around a small green object during a group activity
summary: Simple questions can help a child explain what they noticed, what they tried and what they want to explore next.

sections.heading: Invite an explanation
sections.text: Instead of asking only whether a project worked, ask what the child was trying to make happen. What part was interesting? What surprised them? Giving them time to explain can reveal the thinking behind a build, even when it is still unfinished.

sections.heading: Let the next question stay open
sections.text: You do not need to supply every technical answer to support curiosity. Ask what they might try next and how they could compare the results. For guidance on suitable learning opportunities, talk with the academy about your child’s interests and experience.

author: RobotYOUNG Academy
title: Good ideas begin with a closer look.
alt: A learner concentrating on a circuit board on a blue work mat while an instructor stands nearby
summary: Looking carefully, comparing a plan and asking for guidance are useful habits for any hands-on technology project.

sections.heading: Pause and compare
sections.text: Before moving to the next step, compare the build with the instructions. Notice the position of parts, the order of connections and any details that are easy to overlook. A brief pause can turn an assumption into something you can check.

sections.heading: Make questions specific
sections.text: A question such as ‘Does this connection match the diagram?’ gives a teammate or instructor a clear place to begin. Careful observation and focused questions work together: one helps you notice a detail, and the other helps you understand it.
